definition: Attention replacements built on long implicit convolutions evaluated via FFT, achieving subquadratic sequence mixing.
details: Attention replacements built on long implicit convolutions evaluated via FFT, achieving subquadratic sequence mixing. The research thread that, together with S4, led directly into the Mamba-era state space boom (see State Space Models).

explainer.lead: Hyena and H3 are sequence-mixing layers that replace attention with long implicit convolutions computed via FFT, giving subquadratic cost. They matter as a bridge from convolution-era ideas into the state space model boom.

tiers.eli5: Instead of every word looking at every other word, these layers let each word blend with a long stretch of neighbours in one cheap sweep.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use Hyena/H3-style layers when sequences are too long for attention's quadratic memory, computing convolutions in the frequency domain. Pitfall: FFT-based paths add implementation complexity and can underperform well-tuned attention at moderate lengths.
tiers.paperLevel: Sequence mixing is expressed as long implicit convolutions combined with elementwise gating; the convolutions are evaluated in O(n log n) via the fast Fourier transform, so no explicit n-by-n attention matrix exists. Limits: gains depend on hardware-efficient FFT kernels and comparisons against strong attention baselines.

explainer.example: On a very long document, an H3 layer convolves the whole token sequence in the frequency domain rather than building an n-by-n attention matrix, keeping cost near n log n.
